title: Hugo's Brush Game
markdown:
Hugo the toy fixer had a workshop smelling of paint and wood. Bloom the bee and Miss Maple the squirrel arrived with a flutter.

“Hugo!” buzzed Bloom. “It’s time for a game! But my mouth feels fuzzy, like soft moss on my teeth!”

“Mine too!” squeaked Miss Maple. “It feels sticky, like a dewdrop that stayed too long.”

Hugo’s kind eyes crinkled. He picked up a tiny smooth stone. “The sweet treats you ate left bits, like tiny clingy dust,” he showed them. The dust made the stone feel rough. “This is why your mouths feel funny.”

Bloom and Miss Maple looked at each other. Their fuzzy sticky feeling wasn’t fun.

Hugo took a small soft brush, like moss on old trees. He dipped it in water. “Watch,” he whispered. He gently brushed the stone. The dust tumbled away, making it smooth again. “See? The water and brush are like a forest wind, clearing away dust.”

Bloom’s wings buzzed. “So the brush is like a tiny broom for my mouth!”

“And it makes things smooth!” chattered Miss Maple, her tail flicking. “Can we try this clearing game?”

Hugo smiled. He brought out little brushes and a small mirror. Bloom and Miss Maple guided the brushes. With a swish and a rinse, they brushed their own teeth. The fuzzy sticky feeling went away, replaced by a smooth clean feeling. It felt like treasure.

“Hooray!” buzzed Bloom. “The clingy dust is gone!”

“My teeth feel smooth and bright!” declared Miss Maple.

Hugo nodded. Brushing gave their teeth shiny shields to protect them. Those shields helped them chew acorns and share happy smiles.

Miss Maple’s eyes shone. “So if we keep our shields strong, our teeth will be happy for eating and smiling?”

Bloom buzzed thoughtfully. “I like this game! It feels like a clever helper.”

Miss Maple’s tail twitched. “I wonder,” she mused, “what other clever ways we can help our bodies stay strong and happy?”

A clean tooth is a happy tooth, ready for adventures. Hugo set the little brushes by the mirror, and the workshop smelled of paint, wood, and a fresh forest wind.
characters: Hugo (a kind-eyed toy fixer), Bloom (a fuzzy-mouthed bee), Maple (a sticky-toothed squirrel)
